evidence: Failing-before run: `uv run --with textual --with pytest --with pytest-xdist python -m pytest tests/test_dashboard_app.py -q -n 4 -k 'waits or running or phase_column'` gave 10 failed, 2 passed. The 2 that passed were the 60-column no-phase case, which held before too, and the --once phase-column guard. The failures were assertion errors plus one TypeError for TaskDetail(running_since=...). After the change, the same command gives 12 passed. tests/test_dashboard_app.py + tests/test_dashboard_view.py + tests/test_dashboard_model.py with -n 4: 225 passed. Full non-tmux suite (`-m 'not tmux' -n 4`): 351 passed. Serial tmux run (`uv run -q --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests -q -m tmux -rf`): 11 passed.
observations: A waiting row's title cell is now a Text: title + "  waits on a, b" (dependency slugs sorted, muted, clips with the title). A running row's status reads "▶ running 14m" via a new elapsed helper that relative_time builds on ("now", "Nm", "Nh"). title_width takes the longest status label (minimum 9). task_columns never returns phase: wide is status, task, wave, assignee; render_once keeps phase at width >= 90. task_cells, title_width and fill_tasks take now (snapshot generated_at). Running time refreshes through the existing 30 s REDRAW_SECONDS reload. Detail: running_since added to TaskDetail in dashboard_model.py (latest assignment, only while running); detail_chips shows "▶ running 48h"; status_chip replaced by status_label. Tests: no-phase-column versions of the narrow/wide/resize tests, test_once_keeps_the_phase_column_when_wide, a waits-running stamped store with a 48h-old assignment driving waits-on, running-row and detail-chip tests, a detail_chips unit test at 14m; helpers _titles strips the waits-on note and the status split takes word [1]. Untracked scripts/session_metrics.py and tests/test_session_metrics.py are not mine and were not committed.
